title: Introducing ShellBench, the benchmark for real-world tasks - OpenClaw Blog

quotes.for: Publication date of the ShellBench announcement.

quotes.text: Shellbench is a new benchmark developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley.
It draws on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to measure how AI agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
quotes.for: Benchmark dataset based on 10 million anonymized interactions.

quotes.text: GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%, followed by Claude Fable 5.2 at 61.9% and GPT-6.1 Sol at 61.4%.
quotes.for: Leading model pass rates on ShellBench.

quotes.text: Across all 53,100 runs, 15.7% failed at least one safety check.
OpenClaw and Pi were effectively tied at the top, just 0.01 percentage points apart.
GPT-6 Astra passed 62.5% of tasks at $1.10 per run, Claude Fable 5.2 passed 61.9% at $0.83, and GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% at $0.19.
quotes.for: Pass rates and estimated costs per run across top models.

title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life | TechCrunch

quotes.text: According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time.
When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.
When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts.
quotes.for: Failure to withhold sensitive bank upload token.

quotes.text: The benchmark finds that, on average, even agents powered by the leading models fail to fully complete four out of every ten tasks.

quotes.text: In one assignment involving dinner plans, agents selected the correct restaurant in 522 of 531 attempts.

title: OpenClaw launches an AI performance benchmark that it argues is more realistic than others – Computerworld

quotes.text: Thomas Randall, a research director at Infotech, said that he sees ShellBench as focusing on those who are building and configuring agents directly, but most enterprises instead buy their AI capabilities from various large AI vendors.
